text:
morgan: heads up, autoscaler alerted — queue depth in us-west spiked and GPU util is weirdly low (~18%). looks like a head-of-line issue, small quick inferences stuck behind a few huge batched jobs. :frowning_face:

devon: ugh. seeing the same in the dashboard. per-node GPU % is 10-30% on affected racks while queue backlog is 4k+. traces point at admission-controller holding onto gang allocations for long-lived batch jobs.

priya: can you paste the admission logs? I want to check if preemption timers are firing or if admission is blocked by a lock.

devon: pasted below — pattern looks like repeated admission retries + same gang id blocking the head of queue:

```
I0318 12:04:15.123 admission.go:432] AdmitRequest req=R-2234 model=fast-embed gang=G-998 status=waiting
I0318 12:04:15.456 admission.go:498] AdmitWait start gang=G-998 nodeAffinity=zone:us-west-2a
I0318 12:04:22.990 admission.go:505] AdmitRetry gang=G-998 reason=capacity-mismatch tries=12
I0318 12:04:45.001 dispatcher.go:210] Dispatch skipped gang=G-998 size=32 state=pinned
```

morgan: that `state=pinned` bit is suspicious — possible leftover pin after a failed placement. I remember a recent scheduler change to affinity rotation.

aj: we rolled affinity-rotation v1.7 last week (scheduler) — could be interaction with the gang allocator. if pinned gangs don't time out, they block the admission queue head.

sam: quick mitigation: can we soft-fail pinned gangs older than X seconds and let smaller requests proceed? even a temporary TTL might free the queue.

priya: agreed. pragmatic emergency patch: treat pinned gangs > 20s as preemptable and requeue. also enforce max-concurrency-per-tenant for large batch jobs to avoid head-of-line swings.

devon: i'll open a hotfix PR that adds TTL-based release and a metric for stale-pinned-gangs. will also add a feature-flag so we can rollback quickly.

morgan: also consider rebalancing admission order by request age + size (age-priority) so long-lived queued jobs don't starve fast paths. but that's more of a follow-up.

aj: for immediate relief, i'll push the hotfix behind a FF to canary us-west only, and add a short-rate-limit on large jobs from top tenants. that should lower head-of-line probability.

infra-bot: deploy started: scheduler/v1.7.1-hotfix -> canary (us-west) by aj at 12:27 UTC. CI: green.

devon: hotfix PR: https://git.internal/redwood/scheduler/pull/582 — adds `PinnedGangTTL=20s` + metric `scheduler_pinned_gang_stale_total`.

sam: we should also run a targeted job to flush any stale pins on nodes. I'll run `infractl scheduler flush-pins --zone us-west-2a` in a minute.

morgan: thanks. once canary looks good, roll to 2 more racks. keep an eye on GPU utilization and queue depth; we want small requests throughput to recover.

priya: follow-up postmortem note: scheduler should never leave a pin without heartbeat; add unit tests for pin lifecycle and a dashboard for pin age percentiles.

devon: for monitoring: alert if median queue wait > 300ms for requests < 1s and GPU utilization < 40% across a rack — that indicates head-of-line. I'll add that.

morgan: good. filed incident ticket INF-2026 and added runbook steps (canary hotfix, flush-pins, throttle large jobs). thanks everyone :thumbsup:
